records.source: עַל־מִשְׁכָּבִי֙ בַּלֵּיל֔וֹת בִּקַּ֕שְׁתִּי אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א מְצָאתִֽיו׃
records.gloss: On my bed in the nights I sought him whom my soul loves; I sought him but did not find him.
pieces: Night after night on my bed \q I looked for the one my soul loves; \q I looked for him but did not find him.

L.1: On my bed through the nights \q I sought the one whom my soul loves; \q I sought him, but I did not find him.

R.1: Night after night on my bed \q I looked for the one I love with all my heart. \q I looked for him, but I could not find him.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks (3:1-5)
decisions.reason: She speaks of "my bed" and of the one "my soul loves" (1:7), who is "him"; in 3:4 she brings him to her mother's house.

decisions.choice: in the nights: night after night, or in the night
decisions.reason: The plural may mean night after night, or simply "by night" (Psalm 16:7; 134:1).

decisions.choice: a search that begins on her bed
decisions.reason: She longs for him as she lies in bed and then goes out to look for him (3:2). The scene may be a dream, as 5:2 seems to be, or a story told of her longing; the poem does not say which.

decisions.choice: the one my soul loves
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the phrase of 1:7 and drops "whom", as natural English does.

decisions.choice: the one I love with all my heart

records.heading: A search by night

records.source: אָק֨וּמָה נָּ֜א וַאֲסוֹבְבָ֣ה בָעִ֗יר בַּשְּׁוָקִים֙ וּבָ֣רְחֹב֔וֹת אֲבַקְשָׁ֕ה אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א מְצָאתִֽיו׃
records.gloss: Let me rise now and go about in the city, in the streets and in the squares; let me seek him whom my soul loves; I sought him but did not find him.
pieces: I will get up now and go around the city, \q through the streets and the squares; \q I will search for the one my soul loves. \q I searched for him but did not find him.

L.2: I will rise now and go about in the city, \q in the streets and in the broad places; \q I will seek the one whom my soul loves. \q I sought him, but I did not find him.

R.2: I will get up now and go out into the city, \q through the streets and the squares. \q I will look for the one I love with all my heart. \q I looked for him, but I could not find him.

decisions.choice: I will rise ... I will seek: what she tells herself
decisions.reason: The verbs have the form of resolve, "let me get up": she speaks to herself and then goes.

decisions.choice: the streets and the squares: the open places of the city
decisions.reason: The squares were the open spaces near the gates where people met. A young woman alone in them at night was out of place and unprotected (5:7).

records.source: מְצָא֨וּנִי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים הַסֹּבְבִ֖ים בָּעִ֑יר אֵ֛ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י רְאִיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Found me the watchmen who go about in the city: him whom my soul loves have you seen?
pieces: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. \q "Have you seen the one my soul loves?"

L.3: The watchmen who go about in the city found me. \q "The one whom my soul loves, have you seen [him]?"

R.3: The guards found me as they walked around the city. \q I asked them, "Have you seen the one I love with all my heart?"

decisions.choice: the watchmen: the city guard
decisions.reason: Watchmen kept the walls and gates and walked the streets at night (Psalm 127:1; Isaiah 62:6).

decisions.choice: her question to the watchmen
decisions.reason: She tells what happened and quotes her own question to them; the verb "have you seen" is plural. Her words are given as speech quoted inside her speech.

decisions.choice: quotation marks
decisions.reason: Her question is a speech quoted within her own speech, so it takes double quotation marks, as 2:10-13.

decisions.choice: I asked them
decisions.reason: Readable says that she asked; the Hebrew gives the question without a verb of speaking.

records.source: כִּמְעַט֙ שֶׁעָבַ֣רְתִּי מֵהֶ֔ם עַ֣ד שֶֽׁמָּצָ֔אתִי אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י אֲחַזְתִּיו֙ וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֔נּוּ עַד־שֶׁ֤הֲבֵיאתִיו֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית אִמִּ֔י וְאֶל־חֶ֖דֶר הוֹרָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Scarcely had I passed from them when I found him whom my soul loves; I held him and would not let him go until I had brought him into [the] house of my mother and into [the] room of her who conceived me.
pieces: I had hardly passed them \q when I found the one my soul loves. \q I took hold of him and did not let go of him \q until I had brought him home to my mother's house, \q into the bedroom of the one who conceived me.

L.4: Scarcely had I passed from them, \q when I found the one whom my soul loves. \q I grasped him and did not let him go, \q until I brought him into the house of my mother, \q and into the room of her who conceived me.

R.4: I had only just gone past them \q when I found the one I love with all my heart. \q I held on to him and would not let him go. \q I brought him to my mother's house, \q into the room where my mother conceived me.

decisions.choice: my mother's house: her home, the place for marriage
decisions.reason: A young woman's home could be called her mother's house (Genesis 24:28; Ruth 1:8). There love was to be made lasting; she brings him home (8:2).

decisions.choice: the room of her who conceived me: the place where her own life began
decisions.reason: The inner room is her mother's bedroom. The phrase links her love with her mother's love and with new life (8:5).

decisions.choice: I held him and would not let him go
decisions.reason: She clings to him: having searched so long, she will not lose him again.

records.source: הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה אִם־תָּעִ֧ירוּ׀וְֽאִם־תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ס
records.gloss: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by [the] gazelles or by [the] does of the field: if you stir up and if you awaken the love until it pleases.
pieces: Swear to me, women of Jerusalem, by the gazelles \q or by the does in the fields: \q do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.

L.5: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles \q or by the does of the field: \q do not stir up and do not awaken love until it pleases.

R.5: Women of Jerusalem, promise me \q by the gazelles and the wild deer: \q Do not stir up love or wake it until the time is right.

decisions.choice: the oath of 2:7 repeated
decisions.reason: The words are the same as in 2:7; see the decisions there on the oath, the gazelles and the meaning of "until it pleases". The oath closes the scene of the night search.

decisions.choice: do not stir up love until it pleases: do not rouse love before its time
alternatives: do not disturb the lovers until they wish
decisions.reason: As in 2:7: love should not be awakened before it is ready, or the lovers should not be disturbed.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:7
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded exactly as in 2:7 at each level.

records.source: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן־הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר כְּתִֽימֲר֖וֹת עָשָׁ֑ן מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת מוֹר֙ וּלְבוֹנָ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל אַבְקַ֥ת רוֹכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Who [is] this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed [with] myrrh and frankincense, from all [the] powders of [the] merchant?
pieces: Who is this coming up from the desert \q like columns of smoke, \q fragrant with myrrh and frankincense, \q with every spice the merchants sell?

L.6: Who [is] this coming up from the wilderness \q like columns of smoke, \q perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, \q with all the powders of the merchant?

R.6: Who is this coming up from the desert \q like clouds of smoke, \q with the sweet smell of myrrh and frankincense \q and all the spices that traders sell?

decisions.choice: a new voice asks: the speaker is not named
decisions.reason: The question has no "I" or "we". It may be the women of Jerusalem, onlookers, or the poet; the woman may also be speaking. The same question is asked in 6:10 and 8:5.

decisions.choice: who is this: the woman, or the procession
decisions.reason: "This" and "coming up" are feminine. They may point to a woman, the bride brought in the procession, or to the litter of 3:7, whose name is also feminine. In 8:5 the same words are clearly about the woman.

decisions.choice: columns of smoke ... myrrh and frankincense: a fragrant procession
decisions.reason: Clouds of dust and the smoke of incense rise over the procession as it comes from the open country toward the city. Frankincense is a white resin from trees of southern Arabia, burned for its scent (Exodus 30:34; Isaiah 60:6); myrrh as 1:13.

decisions.choice: the powders of the merchant: imported spices
decisions.reason: Fine perfumed powders sold by traders, who brought spices from far away (Ezekiel 27:22).

records.heading: A procession from the wilderness

records.source: הִנֵּ֗ה מִטָּתוֹ֙ שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שִׁשִּׁ֥ים גִּבֹּרִ֖ים סָבִ֣יב לָ֑הּ מִגִּבֹּרֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Look, his litter, that of Solomon; sixty warriors around it from [the] warriors of Israel.
pieces: Look! It is Solomon's litter, \q surrounded by sixty warriors, \q the best of Israel's warriors.

L.7: Look, his litter, the one of Solomon! \q Sixty warriors [are] around it, \q from the warriors of Israel.

R.7: Look! It is Solomon's carriage, \q with sixty soldiers around it, \q the bravest soldiers in Israel.

decisions.choice: his litter: a couch carried on poles
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a bed or couch; here it is a couch carried by bearers, in which a king or a bride was brought in procession.

decisions.choice: his litter, the one of Solomon: "Solomon's own"
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "his litter" and then names him, which gives emphasis. Whether this Solomon is the king himself, or the beloved pictured as a king (1:4), the poem does not say.

decisions.choice: warriors: the best fighting men
decisions.reason: The word means strong, proven men of war; the guard is the pick of Israel's soldiers.

decisions.choice: carriage
decisions.reason: Readable says "carriage", a word younger readers know, for a couch carried on poles (m1).

records.source: כֻּלָּם֙אֲחֻ֣זֵי חֶ֔רֶב מְלֻמְּדֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה אִ֤ישׁ חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל־יְרֵכ֔וֹ מִפַּ֖חַד בַּלֵּילּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: All of them holding [the] sword, trained of war, each his sword on his thigh, against terror in the nights.
pieces: All of them carry swords \q and are trained for battle, \q each with his sword at his side \q against the dangers of the night.

L.8: All of them hold swords, \q trained in war; \q each [has] his sword at his thigh \q against the terror of the nights.

R.8: Every one of them has a sword \q and is trained to fight. \q Each one wears his sword at his side, \q ready for any danger in the night.

decisions.choice: holding swords: armed and skilled with the sword
decisions.reason: The form can mean "grasped by the sword", that is, practiced in its use, or simply "carrying swords".

decisions.choice: the terror of the nights: dangers in the dark
decisions.reason: Robbers and attackers were feared at night (Psalm 91:5). The guards protect the procession on the road.

decisions.choice: at his side
decisions.reason: The sword hung at the thigh (Judges 3:16); Balanced and Readable say "side".

records.source: אַפִּרְי֗וֹן עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵעֲצֵ֖י הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: A carriage made for himself the king Solomon from [the] wood of the Lebanon.
pieces: King Solomon made himself a carriage \q from the wood of Lebanon.

L.9: A carriage the king Solomon made for himself \q from the wood of Lebanon.

R.9: King Solomon made a carriage for himself \q out of wood from Lebanon.

decisions.choice: a carriage: a canopied chair or couch carried by bearers
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is probably a borrowed word for a grand carried seat, a palanquin.

decisions.choice: Lebanon: the mountains north of Israel
decisions.reason: The Lebanon range was famous for its cedars and pines, the finest building wood, which Solomon used for the temple and his palace (1 Kings 5:20-24; 7:2).

records.source: עַמּוּדָיו֙ עָ֣שָׂה כֶ֔סֶף רְפִידָת֣וֹ זָהָ֔ב מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ אַרְגָּמָ֑ן תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: Its posts he made [of] silver, its back [of] gold, its seat [of] purple; its interior inlaid [with] love by [the] daughters of Jerusalem.
pieces: He made its posts of silver, \q its back of gold, \q its seat of purple cloth; \q its inside was lovingly decorated \q by the women of Jerusalem.

L.10: Its posts he made [of] silver, \q its back [of] gold, \q its seat [of] purple; \q its interior inlaid [with] love \q by the daughters of Jerusalem.

R.10: Its posts were made of silver, \q its back of gold, \q and its seat of purple cloth. \q Its inside was lovingly decorated \q by the women of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: silver, gold and purple: a royal seat
decisions.reason: Purple cloth was dyed with a costly dye from sea snails and was worn by kings (Judges 8:26).

decisions.choice: its back
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here; it means a support, the back or the base of the seat.

decisions.choice: inlaid with love by the women of Jerusalem: lovingly made by them
alternatives: with scenes of love, for the daughters of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The phrase is hard. It may mean that the women of Jerusalem decorated the inside with love, as a gift; or that it was decorated with scenes of love. Some read the word for "love" as the name of a material ("ebony" or "leather"), with a small change. Some take "daughters of Jerusalem" as the start of 3:11.

decisions.choice: lovingly decorated by the women of Jerusalem
alternatives: inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likelier sense (m3) and say "women of Jerusalem" (1:5).

records.source: צְאֶ֧ינָה׀וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בָּעֲטָרָ֗ה שֶׁעִטְּרָה־לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ בְּי֣וֹם חֲתֻנָּת֔וֹ וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: Go out and look, daughters of Zion, at the king Solomon, at the crown with which crowned him his mother on [the] day of his wedding and on [the] day of [the] gladness of his heart.
pieces: Come out, women of Zion, and look at King Solomon, \q at the crown his mother placed on his head on his wedding day, \q the day his heart was glad.

L.11: Go out and look, daughters of Zion, at the king Solomon, \q at the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, \q and on the day of the gladness of his heart.

R.11: Women of Zion, come out and look at King Solomon! \q He is wearing the crown his mother put on his head on his wedding day, \q the day he was so happy.

decisions.choice: the speaker calls the women of Zion
decisions.reason: The commands are feminine plural. The one who calls is the voice of 3:6, or the woman; it is not named.

decisions.choice: daughters of Zion: the women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem, and "daughters of Zion" are its women, the same group as the daughters of Jerusalem (Isaiah 3:16).

decisions.choice: the crown his mother gave him: a wedding crown
decisions.reason: A bridegroom wore a crown or garland at his wedding (Isaiah 61:10). The crowning by his mother is mentioned only here. This is the one time the Song names a wedding.

decisions.choice: women of Zion
decisions.reason: As "women of Jerusalem" (1:5).
